sanskrit.deva:
ॐ भद्रं कर्णेभिः शृणुयाम देवा भद्रं पश्येमाक्षभिर्यजत्राः ।
स्थिरैरङ्गैस्तुष्टुवांसस्तनूभिर्व्यशेम देवहितं यदायुः ॥
स्वस्ति न इन्द्रो वृद्धश्रवाः स्वस्ति नः पूषा विश्ववेदाः ।
स्वस्ति नस्तार्क्ष्यो अरिष्टनेमिः स्वस्ति नो बृहस्पतिर्दधातु ॥
ॐ शान्तिः शान्तिः शान्तिः ॥

words.meaning: O you who are worthy of worship

grammar.en: past active participle m. nom. pl.

closing.translation: Om. May we hear with our ears what is auspicious, O gods; may we see with our eyes what is auspicious, O you who are worthy of worship. Praising you with firm limbs and bodies, may we attain the life that the gods have appointed. May Indra of great fame grant us well-being; may Pūṣan who knows all grant us well-being; may Tārkṣya of the unharmed wheel-rim grant us well-being; may Bṛhaspati grant us well-being. Om. Peace, peace, peace.
notes: The peace invocation of the Upaniṣads of the Atharvaveda. The 1910 edition does not print it with the Muṇḍaka; the text is that of the GRETIL Praśnopaniṣad, as on the Praśna page. Śaṅkara's bhāṣya does not comment on it; the translation gives the plain sense of the words.

sanskrit.deva:
स वेदैतत्परमं ब्रह्म धाम यत्र विश्वं निहितं भाति शुभ्रम् ।
उपासते पुरुषं ये ह्यकामास्ते शुक्रमेतदतिवर्तन्ति धीराः ॥ १ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sa vedaitat paramaṃ brahma dhāma yatra viśvaṃ nihitaṃ bhāti śubhram |
upāsate puruṣaṃ ye hy akāmās te śukram etad ativartanti dhīrāḥ || 1 ||

lines.iast: sa vedaitat paramaṃ brahma dhāma yatra viśvaṃ nihitaṃ bhāti śubhram
lines.deva: स वेदैतत्परमं ब्रह्म धाम यत्र विश्वं निहितं भाति शुभ्रम्

lines.iast: upāsate puruṣaṃ ye hy akāmās te śukram etad ativartanti dhīrāḥ
lines.deva: उपासते पुरुषं ये ह्यकामास्ते शुक्रमेतदतिवर्तन्ति धीराः

padaccheda.iast: saḥ veda etat paramam brahma dhāma yatra viśvam nihitam bhāti śubhram upāsate puruṣam ye hi akāmāḥ te śukram etat ativartanti dhīrāḥ
padaccheda.deva: सः वेद एतत् परमम् ब्रह्म धाम यत्र विश्वम् निहितम् भाति शुभ्रम् उपासते पुरुषम् ये हि अकामाः ते शुक्रम् एतत् अतिवर्तन्ति धीराः

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: He (the knower of the Self) knows this supreme Brahman, the abode, in which the universe is set and which shines pure. The wise who, free from desire, worship that man pass beyond this seed (of birth).

notes: Śaṅkara: because the knower of the Self knows this Brahman as described, the supreme abode, the ground of all desires, in which the whole world is set, and which shines pure by its own light: those who, free of desire, without thirst for prosperity, seeking liberation, worship such a man, the knower of the Self, as if he were the supreme god, pass beyond this well-known seed of man, the material cause of the body; the wise do not go to a womb again. So the sense is: one should honour him.

sanskrit.deva:
कामान्यः कामयते मन्यमानः स कामभिर्जायते तत्र तत्र ।
पर्याप्तकामस्य कृतात्मनस्तु इहैव सर्वे प्रविलीयन्ति कामाः ॥ २ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
kāmān yaḥ kāmayate manyamānaḥ sa kāmabhir jāyate tatra tatra |
paryāptakāmasya kṛtātmanas tu ihaiva sarve pravilīyanti kāmāḥ || 2 ||

lines.iast: kāmān yaḥ kāmayate manyamānaḥ sa kāmabhir jāyate tatra tatra
lines.deva: कामान्यः कामयते मन्यमानः स कामभिर्जायते तत्र तत्र

lines.iast: paryāptakāmasya kṛtātmanas tu ihaiva sarve pravilīyanti kāmāḥ
lines.deva: पर्याप्तकामस्य कृतात्मनस्तु इहैव सर्वे प्रविलीयन्ति कामाः

padaccheda.iast: kāmān yaḥ kāmayate manyamānaḥ saḥ kāmabhiḥ jāyate tatra tatra paryāpta-kāmasya kṛta-ātmanaḥ tu iha eva sarve pravilīyanti kāmāḥ
padaccheda.deva: कामान् यः कामयते मन्यमानः सः कामभिः जायते तत्र तत्र पर्याप्त-कामस्य कृत-आत्मनः तु इह एव सर्वे प्रविलीयन्ति कामाः

words.meaning: of him whose desires are fulfilled

translations.text: He who desires objects, dwelling on them, is born with those desires here and there. But for him whose desires are fulfilled, whose self is accomplished, all desires dissolve here itself.

notes: Śaṅkara: this shows that for the seeker of liberation the giving up of desire is the chief means. He who desires objects, seen and unseen, dwelling on their merits, is born with those desires, which are the wish for objects and the causes of acting by dharma and adharma; wherever desires set a man to action for gaining objects, there he is born among those objects, wrapped in those same desires. But he whose desires are all fulfilled, because by knowing the highest truth he desires the Self, and whose self has been made by knowledge into its own supreme form, taken away from the lower form that is ignorance: for him all desires, the causes of acting by dharma and adharma, dissolve here itself, while he still stands in the body; their cause being destroyed, they do not arise.

sanskrit.deva:
नायमात्मा प्रवचनेन लभ्यो न मेधया न बहुना श्रुतेन ।
यमेवैष वृणुते तेन लभ्यस्तस्यैष आत्मा विवृणुते तनूं स्वाम् ॥ ३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
nāyam ātmā pravacanena labhyo na medhayā na bahunā śrutena |
yam evaiṣa vṛṇute tena labhyas tasyaiṣa ātmā vivṛṇute tanūṃ svām || 3 ||

lines.iast: nāyam ātmā pravacanena labhyo na medhayā na bahunā śrutena
lines.deva: नायमात्मा प्रवचनेन लभ्यो न मेधया न बहुना श्रुतेन

lines.iast: yam evaiṣa vṛṇute tena labhyas tasyaiṣa ātmā vivṛṇute tanūṃ svām
lines.deva: यमेवैष वृणुते तेन लभ्यस्तस्यैष आत्मा विवृणुते तनूं स्वाम्

padaccheda.iast: na ayam ātmā pravacanena labhyaḥ na medhayā na bahunā śrutena yam eva eṣaḥ vṛṇute tena labhyaḥ tasya eṣaḥ ātmā vivṛṇute tanūm svām
padaccheda.deva: न अयम् आत्मा प्रवचनेन लभ्यः न मेधया न बहुना श्रुतेन यम् एव एषः वृणुते तेन लभ्यः तस्य एषः आत्मा विवृणुते तनूम् स्वाम्

translations.text: This Self is not gained by teaching, nor by intelligence, nor by much learning. It is gained by that alone, by the seeker's choosing it alone; to him this Self reveals its own nature.

notes: Śaṅkara: if the gaining of the Self is the highest of all gains, it might be thought that teaching and the other means should be used in plenty to gain it; to that the mantra says: this Self, whose gaining is the highest human end, is not gained by pravacana, much study of the Vedas and śāstras; nor by medhā, the power of holding the meaning of books; nor by much hearing. By what then? The supreme Self which alone this knower chooses, wishes to reach: by that choosing it is gained, by no other means, since it is by nature ever gained. To him the Self reveals its own supreme nature, hidden by ignorance; it shows itself when knowledge is there, as a pot appears when there is light. So praying for the Self alone, giving up all else, is the means of gaining it.

sanskrit.deva:
नायमात्मा बलहीनेन लभ्यो न च प्रमादात्तपसो वाप्यलिङ्गात् ।
एतैरुपायैर्यतते यस्तु विद्वांस्तस्यैष आत्मा विशते ब्रह्म धाम ॥ ४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
nāyam ātmā balahīnena labhyo na ca pramādāt tapaso vāpy aliṅgāt |
etair upāyair yatate yas tu vidvāṃs tasyaiṣa ātmā viśate brahma dhāma || 4 ||

lines.iast: nāyam ātmā balahīnena labhyo na ca pramādāt tapaso vāpy aliṅgāt
lines.deva: नायमात्मा बलहीनेन लभ्यो न च प्रमादात्तपसो वाप्यलिङ्गात्

lines.iast: etair upāyair yatate yas tu vidvāṃs tasyaiṣa ātmā viśate brahma dhāma
lines.deva: एतैरुपायैर्यतते यस्तु विद्वांस्तस्यैष आत्मा विशते ब्रह्म धाम

padaccheda.iast: na ayam ātmā bala-hīnena labhyaḥ na ca pramādāt tapasaḥ vā api aliṅgāt etaiḥ upāyaiḥ yatate yaḥ tu vidvān tasya eṣaḥ ātmā viśate brahma dhāma
padaccheda.deva: न अयम् आत्मा बल-हीनेन लभ्यः न च प्रमादात् तपसः वा अपि अलिङ्गात् एतैः उपायैः यतते यः तु विद्वान् तस्य एषः आत्मा विशते ब्रह्म धाम

grammar.en: past active participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: This Self is not gained by one without strength, nor through heedlessness, nor through austerity (knowledge) without its mark (renunciation). But the wise man who strives by these means: his self enters Brahman, the abode.

notes: Śaṅkara: these means help the prayer for the Self: strength, heedfulness and austerity joined with its mark, renunciation. balahīna: without the strength born of steadfastness in the Self. pramāda: the heedlessness that comes of worldly attachment to sons, cattle and the like. tapas here is knowledge, liṅga is renunciation: the Self is not gained by knowledge without renunciation. The discerning knower of the Self who strives, intent on it, by these means, strength, heedfulness, renunciation and knowledge: his self enters Brahman, the abode.

sanskrit.deva:
संप्राप्यैनमृषयो ज्ञानतृप्ताः कृतात्मानो वीतरागाः प्रशान्ताः ।
ते सर्वगं सर्वतः प्राप्य धीरा युक्तात्मानः सर्वमेवाविशन्ति ॥ ५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
saṃprāpyainam ṛṣayo jñānatṛptāḥ kṛtātmāno vītarāgāḥ praśāntāḥ |
te sarvagaṃ sarvataḥ prāpya dhīrā yuktātmānaḥ sarvam evāviśanti || 5 ||

lines.iast: saṃprāpyainam ṛṣayo jñānatṛptāḥ kṛtātmāno vītarāgāḥ praśāntāḥ
lines.deva: संप्राप्यैनमृषयो ज्ञानतृप्ताः कृतात्मानो वीतरागाः प्रशान्ताः

lines.iast: te sarvagaṃ sarvataḥ prāpya dhīrā yuktātmānaḥ sarvam evāviśanti
lines.deva: ते सर्वगं सर्वतः प्राप्य धीरा युक्तात्मानः सर्वमेवाविशन्ति

padaccheda.iast: saṃprāpya enam ṛṣayaḥ jñāna-tṛptāḥ kṛta-ātmānaḥ vīta-rāgāḥ praśāntāḥ te sarvagam sarvataḥ prāpya dhīrāḥ yukta-ātmānaḥ sarvam eva āviśanti
padaccheda.deva: संप्राप्य एनम् ऋषयः ज्ञान-तृप्ताः कृत-आत्मानः वीत-रागाः प्रशान्ताः ते सर्वगम् सर्वतः प्राप्य धीराः युक्त-आत्मानः सर्वम् एव आविशन्ति

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. pl.

translations.text: Having reached him, the seers, content with knowledge, their selves accomplished, free from passion, tranquil: these wise ones, collected, having reached the all-pervading everywhere, enter the All.

notes: Śaṅkara: how they enter Brahman: having fully known this Self, the seers, men of vision, are content with that knowledge alone, not with outward means of contentment that feed the body; their selves accomplished in the very nature of the supreme Self; free of passion and the other faults; tranquil, their senses withdrawn. Having reached the all-pervading, like space, everywhere, not with a part bounded by adjuncts, but realizing that non-dual Brahman itself as the Self, the wise, wholly discerning, ever collected by nature, enter the All even at the fall of the body: they give up the limits of the adjuncts made by ignorance, as the space in a pot when the pot is broken. So the knowers of Brahman enter Brahman, the abode.

sanskrit.deva:
वेदान्तविज्ञानसुनिश्चितार्थाः संन्यासयोगाद्यतयः शुद्धसत्त्वाः ।
ते ब्रह्मलोकेषु परान्तकाले परामृताः परिमुच्यन्ति सर्वे ॥ ६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
vedāntavijñānasuniścitārthāḥ saṃnyāsayogād yatayaḥ śuddhasattvāḥ |
te brahmalokeṣu parāntakāle parāmṛtāḥ parimucyanti sarve || 6 ||

lines.iast: vedāntavijñānasuniścitārthāḥ saṃnyāsayogād yatayaḥ śuddhasattvāḥ
lines.deva: वेदान्तविज्ञानसुनिश्चितार्थाः संन्यासयोगाद्यतयः शुद्धसत्त्वाः

lines.iast: te brahmalokeṣu parāntakāle parāmṛtāḥ parimucyanti sarve
lines.deva: ते ब्रह्मलोकेषु परान्तकाले परामृताः परिमुच्यन्ति सर्वे

padaccheda.iast: vedānta-vijñāna-suniścita-arthāḥ saṃnyāsa-yogāt yatayaḥ śuddha-sattvāḥ te brahma-lokeṣu parāntakāle parāmṛtāḥ parimucyanti sarve
padaccheda.deva: वेदान्त-विज्ञान-सुनिश्चित-अर्थाः संन्यास-योगात् यतयः शुद्ध-सत्त्वाः ते ब्रह्म-लोकेषु परान्तकाले परामृताः परिमुच्यन्ति सर्वे

words.meaning: sure of the meaning of the knowledge of the Vedānta

translations.text: The renouncers who are sure of the meaning of the knowledge of the Vedānta, pure in mind through the yoga of renunciation: at the final end (the last falling of the body) they all, immortal as Brahman, are wholly freed in Brahman.

notes: Śaṅkara: vedāntavijñāna: the knowledge born of the Vedānta; its meaning, the supreme Self to be known, they have well ascertained. saṃnyāsayoga: the yoga that is the giving up of all rites, resting in Brahman alone; by it they are yatis, given to striving, pure in mind. parāntakāla: the times of death of those in the round are ‘ends’ that are not final; compared with them, for seekers of liberation the time of leaving the body at the close of the round is the final end. brahmalokeṣu: Brahman itself is the world, brahmaloka; the plural is because the seekers are many, and the one is seen and reached as if many; so ‘in Brahman’. parāmṛtāḥ: those whose self is the supreme immortal, Brahman, become Brahman while still living. parimucyanti: they cease on every side, like the going out of a lamp or the space in a broken pot; all of them are freed, and need not go to another place.

Śaṅkara, on the same: so scripture and tradition: ‘as the track of birds in the sky or of a fish in water is not seen, so is the going of those who know’ (Mokṣadharma 181.9); ‘not travelling the roads, they cross to the far shore of the roads’. Going bounded by place belongs to the round alone, being the effect of limited means; Brahman, being all, is not to be reached by going to a place. If Brahman were bounded by place it would, like a solid thing, have a beginning and an end, depend on another, have parts, and be impermanent and made; Brahman cannot be such; so reaching it cannot be bounded by place either.

sanskrit.deva:
गताः कलाः पञ्चदश प्रतिष्ठा देवाश्च सर्वे प्रतिदेवतासु ।
कर्माणि विज्ञानमयश्च आत्मा परेऽव्यये सर्व एकीभवन्ति ॥ ७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
gatāḥ kalāḥ pañcadaśa pratiṣṭhā devāś ca sarve pratidevatāsu |
karmāṇi vijñānamayaś ca ātmā pare 'vyaye sarva ekībhavanti || 7 ||

lines.iast: gatāḥ kalāḥ pañcadaśa pratiṣṭhā devāś ca sarve pratidevatāsu
lines.deva: गताः कलाः पञ्चदश प्रतिष्ठा देवाश्च सर्वे प्रतिदेवतासु

lines.iast: karmāṇi vijñānamayaś ca ātmā pare 'vyaye sarva ekībhavanti
lines.deva: कर्माणि विज्ञानमयश्च आत्मा परेऽव्यये सर्व एकीभवन्ति

padaccheda.iast: gatāḥ kalāḥ pañcadaśa pratiṣṭhāḥ devāḥ ca sarve pratidevatāsu karmāṇi vijñānamayaḥ ca ātmā pare avyaye sarve ekībhavanti
padaccheda.deva: गताः कलाः पञ्चदश प्रतिष्ठाः देवाः च सर्वे प्रतिदेवतासु कर्माणि विज्ञानमयः च आत्मा परे अव्यये सर्वे एकीभवन्ति

grammar.en: past passive participle f. nom. pl.

translations.text: The fifteen parts go to their sources, and all the gods (of the senses) into their corresponding deities; the actions, and the self that consists of understanding, all become one in the supreme, the undecaying (Brahman).

notes: Śaṅkara: the knowers of Brahman hold liberation to be only the removal of the bondage of the round, ignorance and the rest, not something produced. At liberation the parts that made up the body, prāṇa and the rest, go to their own sources, each into its cause; pratiṣṭhāḥ is accusative plural. They are the well-known fifteen named in the last question (Praśna 6.4). The gods resting in the body, in the eye and the other organs, go into their corresponding deities, the sun and the rest. karmāṇi: the actions done by the seeker whose fruit has not begun, for those whose fruit has begun are spent by being undergone. vijñānamaya ātmā: the self that, taking as itself the intellect and other adjuncts made by ignorance, has entered here into the various bodies like the reflection of the sun in water and the like; called ‘consisting of understanding’, mostly made of it, since actions are for its fruit. When the adjuncts are removed, all of these become one, without distinction, in the supreme, undecaying, infinite, imperishable Brahman, like space, unborn, ageless, deathless, fearless, without before or after, without inside or outside, non-dual, auspicious, peaceful: as the reflections of the sun become one with the sun when the water is taken away, and the spaces of pots with space when the pots are removed.

sanskrit.deva:
यथा नद्यः स्यन्दमानाः समुद्रेऽस्तं गच्छन्ति नामरूपे विहाय ।
तथा विद्वान्नामरूपाद्विमुक्तः परात्परं पुरुषमुपैति दिव्यम् ॥ ८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yathā nadyaḥ syandamānāḥ samudre 'staṃ gacchanti nāmarūpe vihāya |
tathā vidvān nāmarūpād vimuktaḥ parāt paraṃ puruṣam upaiti divyam || 8 ||

lines.iast: yathā nadyaḥ syandamānāḥ samudre 'staṃ gacchanti nāmarūpe vihāya
lines.deva: यथा नद्यः स्यन्दमानाः समुद्रेऽस्तं गच्छन्ति नामरूपे विहाय

lines.iast: tathā vidvān nāmarūpād vimuktaḥ parāt paraṃ puruṣam upaiti divyam
lines.deva: तथा विद्वान्नामरूपाद्विमुक्तः परात्परं पुरुषमुपैति दिव्यम्

padaccheda.iast: yathā nadyaḥ syandamānāḥ samudre astam gacchanti nāma-rūpe vihāya tathā vidvān nāma-rūpāt vimuktaḥ parāt param puruṣam upaiti divyam
padaccheda.deva: यथा नद्यः स्यन्दमानाः समुद्रे अस्तम् गच्छन्ति नाम-रूपे विहाय तथा विद्वान् नाम-रूपात् विमुक्तः परात् परम् पुरुषम् उपैति दिव्यम्

grammar.en: past active participle m. nom. sg.
past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: As flowing rivers disappear in the sea, leaving name and form, so the knower, freed from name and form, reaches the divine Puruṣa, higher than the high (imperishable).

notes: Śaṅkara: as the rivers, Gaṅgā and the rest, flowing on, reach the sea and go to disappearance, to being without distinction, giving up name and form, so the knower, freed from name and form made by ignorance, reaches the divine Puruṣa, as described, higher than the high imperishable spoken of before (2.1.2).

sanskrit.deva:
स यो ह वै तत्परमं ब्रह्म वेद ब्रह्मैव भवति नास्याब्रह्मवित्कुले भवति ।
तरति शोकं तरति पाप्मानं गुहाग्रन्थिभ्यो विमुक्तोऽमृतो भवति ॥ ९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sa yo ha vai tat paramaṃ brahma veda brahmaiva bhavati nāsyābrahmavit kule bhavati |
tarati śokaṃ tarati pāpmānaṃ guhāgranthibhyo vimukto 'mṛto bhavati || 9 ||

lines.iast: sa yo ha vai tat paramaṃ brahma veda brahmaiva bhavati nāsyābrahmavit kule bhavati
lines.deva: स यो ह वै तत्परमं ब्रह्म वेद ब्रह्मैव भवति नास्याब्रह्मवित्कुले भवति

lines.iast: tarati śokaṃ tarati pāpmānaṃ guhāgranthibhyo vimukto 'mṛto bhavati
lines.deva: तरति शोकं तरति पाप्मानं गुहाग्रन्थिभ्यो विमुक्तोऽमृतो भवति

padaccheda.iast: saḥ yaḥ ha vai tat paramam brahma veda brahma eva bhavati na asya abrahmavit kule bhavati tarati śokam tarati pāpmānam guhā-granthibhyaḥ vimuktaḥ amṛtaḥ bhavati
padaccheda.deva: सः यः ह वै तत् परमम् ब्रह्म वेद ब्रह्म एव भवति न अस्य अब्रह्मवित् कुले भवति तरति शोकम् तरति पाप्मानम् गुहा-ग्रन्थिभ्यः विमुक्तः अमृतः भवति

words.meaning: one who does not know Brahman
from the knots of the cave

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: He who knows that supreme Brahman becomes Brahman itself. In his family none is born who does not know Brahman. He crosses grief, he crosses evil (merit and demerit); freed from the knots of the heart, he becomes immortal.

notes: Śaṅkara, on an objection: many obstacles to the highest good are well known; so even a knower of Brahman, hindered by one of the afflictions or by the gods or another, might go at death to some other state, not to Brahman itself. No: knowledge alone has removed every obstacle. Liberation is kept off only by ignorance, by nothing else, since it is eternal and one's own Self. So whoever in the world knows that supreme Brahman directly as ‘I am that’ goes to no other state; even the gods cannot hinder his reaching Brahman, for he becomes their Self. So the knower of Brahman becomes Brahman itself.

Śaṅkara: in his family no one is born who does not know Brahman. He crosses grief, the pain of mind from the loss of many cherished things, already while living; he crosses evil, called dharma and adharma; freed from the knots of the cave, the knots of ignorance in the heart, he becomes immortal, as was said in ‘the knot of the heart is cut’ (2.2.9).

sanskrit.deva:
तदेतदृचाभ्युक्तम् ।
क्रियावन्तः श्रोत्रिया ब्रह्मनिष्ठाः स्वयं जुह्वत एकर्षिं श्रद्धयन्तः ।
तेषामेवैतां ब्रह्मविद्यां वदेत शिरोव्रतं विधिवद्यैस्तु चीर्णम् ॥ १० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tad etad ṛcābhyuktam |
kriyāvantaḥ śrotriyā brahmaniṣṭhāḥ svayaṃ juhvata ekarṣiṃ śraddhayantaḥ |
teṣām evaitāṃ brahmavidyāṃ vadeta śirovrataṃ vidhivad yais tu cīrṇam || 10 ||

lines.iast: tad etad ṛcābhyuktam
lines.deva: तदेतदृचाभ्युक्तम्

lines.iast: kriyāvantaḥ śrotriyā brahmaniṣṭhāḥ svayaṃ juhvata ekarṣiṃ śraddhayantaḥ
lines.deva: क्रियावन्तः श्रोत्रिया ब्रह्मनिष्ठाः स्वयं जुह्वत एकर्षिं श्रद्धयन्तः

lines.iast: teṣām evaitāṃ brahmavidyāṃ vadeta śirovrataṃ vidhivad yais tu cīrṇam
lines.deva: तेषामेवैतां ब्रह्मविद्यां वदेत शिरोव्रतं विधिवद्यैस्तु चीर्णम्

padaccheda.iast: tat etat ṛcā abhyuktam kriyāvantaḥ śrotriyāḥ brahma-niṣṭhāḥ svayam juhvate ekarṣim śraddhayantaḥ teṣām eva etām brahma-vidyām vadeta śiraḥ-vratam vidhivat yaiḥ tu cīrṇam
padaccheda.deva: तत् एतत् ऋचा अभ्युक्तम् क्रियावन्तः श्रोत्रियाः ब्रह्म-निष्ठाः स्वयम् जुह्वते एकर्षिम् श्रद्धयन्तः तेषाम् एव एताम् ब्रह्म-विद्याम् वदेत शिरः-व्रतम् विधिवत् यैः तु चीर्णम्

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.
past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: This is declared by a verse: ‘To those alone who perform the rites, are versed in the Veda and devoted to (the lower) Brahman, who themselves, with faith, offer into the fire called Ekarṣi, and by whom the vow of the head has been duly kept, one should tell this knowledge of Brahman.’

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the mantra: now the Upaniṣad closes by showing the rule for handing on the knowledge of Brahman; that rule is declared by a verse.

Śaṅkara: kriyāvantaḥ: engaged in doing the rites described. brahmaniṣṭhāḥ: given to the lower Brahman and wishing to know the higher. ekarṣi: the fire named Ekarṣi, into which they themselves offer with faith. To them alone, refined in self and fit vessels, one should tell this knowledge of Brahman; and to those by whom the vow of the head, the carrying of fire on the head, has been duly kept, as is well known among the followers of the Atharvaveda as their Vedic vow.

sanskrit.deva:
तदेतत्सत्यमृषिरङ्गिराः पुरोवाच नैतदचीर्णव्रतोऽधीते ।
नमः परमऋषिभ्यो नमः परमऋषिभ्यः ॥ ११ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tad etat satyam ṛṣir aṅgirāḥ purovāca naitad acīrṇavrato 'dhīte |
namaḥ paramaṛṣibhyo namaḥ paramaṛṣibhyaḥ || 11 ||

lines.iast: tad etat satyam ṛṣir aṅgirāḥ purovāca naitad acīrṇavrato 'dhīte
lines.deva: तदेतत्सत्यमृषिरङ्गिराः पुरोवाच नैतदचीर्णव्रतोऽधीते

lines.iast: namaḥ paramaṛṣibhyo namaḥ paramaṛṣibhyaḥ
lines.deva: नमः परमऋषिभ्यो नमः परमऋषिभ्यः

padaccheda.iast: tat etat satyam ṛṣiḥ aṅgirāḥ purā uvāca na etat acīrṇa-vrataḥ adhīte namaḥ parama-ṛṣibhyaḥ namaḥ parama-ṛṣibhyaḥ
padaccheda.deva: तत् एतत् सत्यम् ऋषिः अङ्गिराः पुरा उवाच न एतत् अचीर्ण-व्रतः अधीते नमः परम-ऋषिभ्यः नमः परम-ऋषिभ्यः

words.meaning: one who has not kept the vow

translations.text: This truth the seer Aṅgiras told of old (to Śaunaka). One who has not kept the vow does not study it. Homage to the supreme seers! Homage to the supreme seers!

notes: Śaṅkara: this imperishable, true Puruṣa the seer Aṅgiras of old told to Śaunaka, who had approached him in due form and asked; so too another should tell it, in the same way, to one who seeks the good, seeks liberation, and has approached him in due form. One who has not kept the vow does not study this even as a text; for only to one who has kept the vow is the knowledge refined to bear fruit. The knowledge of Brahman is complete. Homage to the supreme seers, Brahmā and the others, from whom it has come down in succession, who saw the supreme Brahman directly and knew it; homage again. The repetition is out of great reverence and marks the end of the Upaniṣad.
